decisions.evidence: Round 3 presentation: “Paste a link into the box at the top and press ‘Save.’” Client: “The basic flow feels right.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: URL-based bookmark saving conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 presentation says each item shows only “a title, a short description, and the web address.” Client requests “the page’s actual small site icon and, when available, a preview image.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the initial metadata/list presentation omitted favicon and preview-image behavior; the client supplied the missing requirements.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 presentation has the user press Save before metadata appears, with editing deferred to a later flow. Client calls the basic flow right and raises other additions, but does not request editing title/description before saving.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the presented flow supports post-save editing only, not editing auto-collected title/description before saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 revised presentation adds “the site’s own small icon” and “a preview image.” Client says the saving flow now matches expectations.
decisions.note: Prototype review: revised metadata collection and display conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 presentation says a duplicate only “jump[s] to and highlight[s]” the existing item and that actual editing comes next. Client accepts it only for this step and requires the completed flow to “take me directly into editing it.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: merely highlighting the duplicate did not yet guide the user into editing the existing bookmark.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 revised presentation: pasting an already-saved link takes the user “straight into that bookmark’s editor.” Client: “exactly right.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the revised duplicate-save flow conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 editor presentation lists title, description, note, and tags but no URL field. Client: “I should be able to edit the web address as well.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: editable URL was missing from the presented editor.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 presentation: “Click any saved bookmark. An editor should open.” Client says clicking the title or card should open the original page and asks for a separate Edit action.
decisions.note: Prototype review: list-item selection incorrectly opened the editor instead of navigating to the original URL.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 presentation offers manual chip entry and mentions a pick-from-existing menu only as an alternative. Client requests suggestions from previously used tags while typing.
decisions.note: Prototype review: existing-tag autocomplete was missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 presentation says the note appears in a highlighted block without rendered formatting. Client requests simple Markdown rendering for links and lists.
decisions.note: Prototype review: Markdown rendering was missing from note display.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 presentation allows adding/removing multiple tag chips and displays tags beneath the bookmark. Client keeps the chip style.
decisions.note: Prototype review: tag assignment and per-item tag display conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 revised presentation adds an editable “Web address” field. Client says changing the address completes the editor.
decisions.note: Prototype review: revised bookmark editing conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 revised presentation makes the card/title open the original page and provides a separate Edit button. Client says this is clear.
decisions.note: Prototype review: revised navigation behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 revised presentation supplies matching suggestions from previously used tags. Client: “exactly what I wanted.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: tag autocomplete conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 revised presentation renders bold, italic, links, bullet lists, and inline code. Client explicitly says that Markdown subset is enough.
decisions.note: Prototype review: lightweight Markdown note rendering fulfills the stated requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 presentation adds a per-card “Read later” toggle and “To read” flag. Client approves.
decisions.note: Prototype review: marking a bookmark unread/read-later conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 presentation provides a dedicated “To read” tab containing only marked bookmarks. Client approves.
decisions.note: Prototype review: separate unread view conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 presentation says toggling off removes the item from To read while retaining it in All. Client confirms this expected behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype review: marking read and removing from the unread view conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 presentation searches title, description, note, tags, and URL. Client says the basic search behavior is right.
decisions.note: Prototype review: full-text search across the required bookmark fields conforms; searching tags additionally is not a divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 presents basic search as complete without case-insensitivity. Client: “It should ignore capitalization.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: case-insensitive search was missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 presents ordinary word/tag matching without exact `#tag` syntax. Client requires “`#reading` should specifically mean the `reading` tag.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: exact tag-query syntax was missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 presents word-based search only. Client requires quotation marks to find an exact phrase.
decisions.note: Prototype review: quoted exact-phrase search was missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 supports only implicit multi-word AND. Client requests `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, parentheses, and quoted literal operators.
decisions.note: Prototype review: boolean/grouped search and literal-operator handling were missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 revised presentation verifies `ROME` and `rome` return the same results. Client approves the richer search.
decisions.note: Prototype review: revised case-insensitive search conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 revised presentation makes `#reading` match only the exact tag. Client approves.
decisions.note: Prototype review: revised tag-query syntax conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 revised presentation supports quoted exact phrases. Client approves.
decisions.note: Prototype review: revised phrase search conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 revised presentation supports case-insensitive boolean operators, parentheses, implicit AND, and quoted literal operators. Client approves.
decisions.note: Prototype review: revised advanced search language conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 presentation hides archived items from All and To read while retaining their content. Client confirms that behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype review: archive behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 presentation provides a separate searchable Archived tab. Client approves.
decisions.note: Prototype review: archived-only view conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 presentation makes Archive reversible through Restore. Client says archived links should be easy to restore.
decisions.note: Prototype review: reversible archive behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 presentation: “I did not add any permanent-delete action” and asks whether no delete is right. Client rejects this and requires a separate, confirmed, permanent Delete action in regular and archived views.
decisions.note: Prototype review: explicitly omitting permanent deletion contradicted the delete and archive-versus-delete requirements.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 revised presentation adds permanent deletion in every view with named confirmation and cancellation. Client says this completes the behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype review: revised deletion and archive/delete distinction conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 presentation shows a readability-oriented list with wrapped titles, three-line descriptions, and wrapping tags. Client endorses trimming descriptions.
decisions.note: Prototype review: large-list readability behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 presents a continuously scrolling/searchable large list without ordering controls. Client requests newest/oldest and title A–Z/Z–A, with newest default.
decisions.note: Prototype review: user-selectable sorting was missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 presents tag pills only as displayed content. Client requests clicking a tag pill to show only bookmarks with that tag.
decisions.note: Prototype review: direct tag filtering was missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 revised presentation makes a clicked tag pill run an exact `#tag` filter. Client says it behaves exactly as expected.
decisions.note: Prototype review: revised tag filtering conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 revised presentation offers Newest, Oldest, A–Z, and Z–A; client selects the compact dropdown and accepts newest as the initial default.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the sort capability conforms; the visual control choice is orthogonal.

decisions.evidence: Round 14 presentation re-saving an archived URL opens the existing archived bookmark and offers Restore instead of creating another copy. Client says this is exactly expected.
decisions.note: Prototype review: duplicate handling also conforms for archived bookmarks.

decisions.evidence: Round 16 purported complete scope still separates “paste a link and its…details…are filled in” from later editing and retains the save-first prototype flow. Client identifies several other omissions but does not mention editing metadata before save.
decisions.note: First specification gate: the continuing scope still lacks pre-save title/description editing, and the client does not surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 16 maker says the first version is fully mapped but includes no multi-selection or bulk actions. Client requires selecting several bookmarks for tag, read/unread, archive, and delete actions.
decisions.note: First specification gate: multi-bookmark bulk actions were missing from the proposed complete scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 16 complete scope lacks whole-filter actions. Client asks to apply an action to every bookmark matching the current search/view and nowhere outside it.
decisions.note: First specification gate: filter-scoped whole-collection actions were missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 16 complete scope lacks saved filters. Client requests named, live collections containing search words and included/excluded tags.
decisions.note: First specification gate: bundles/saved filters were missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 16 complete scope lacks preserved copies. Client requests a revisitable page copy and preservation of the PDF itself for PDF URLs.
decisions.note: First specification gate: local snapshot/PDF preservation was missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 16 complete scope lacks external archival. Client requests an option to save through the Internet Archive.
decisions.note: First specification gate: Internet Archive support was missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 16 complete scope lacks import. Client requests importing the usual bookmarks HTML while keeping titles, tags, and saved dates.
decisions.note: First specification gate: Netscape-format import was missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 16 complete scope lacks export. Client requests exporting the collection using standard bookmarks HTML.
decisions.note: First specification gate: Netscape-format export was missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 16 explicitly records default-sort settings for “a later round.” Client rejects that deferral and requires default sort, displayed amount, and font size in this build.
decisions.note: First specification gate: required personal display settings were deferred outside the proposed build.

decisions.evidence: Round 17 revised presentation provides multi-select with add/remove tags, read/unread, archive/restore, and confirmed delete. Client approves.
decisions.note: Prototype review: revised bulk-action behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 17 revised presentation provides “Select all N matching” limited to the current view and search. Client explicitly confirms it must include all matches, including off-screen ones, and leave others untouched.
decisions.note: Prototype review: whole-filter bulk scope conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 18 revised presentation saves a named search using words, included `#tags`, and `NOT` exclusions and re-evaluates it live. Client says this matches the intended named collections.
decisions.note: Prototype review: bundles/saved filters conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 19 presentation chooses “a manual action you trigger per bookmark” for local preservation. Client instead requires automatic capture whenever a new bookmark is saved, with visible failure and retry.
decisions.note: Prototype review: manual-only preservation diverged from automatic on-save preservation.

decisions.evidence: Round 19 presentation preserves the actual PDF for PDF links rather than a page snapshot. Client explicitly confirms this is correct.
decisions.note: Prototype review: PDF preservation rule conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 19 presentation makes Internet Archive submission optional and per-bookmark. Client explicitly approves that separation.
decisions.note: Prototype review: optional Internet Archive support conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 20 revised presentation automatically captures every newly saved page, retains PDFs as PDFs, and shows retryable capture failure. Client says this matches the desired behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype review: revised automatic snapshot/PDF behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 20 revised presentation keeps Internet Archive submission separate, optional, and off by default. Client approves.
decisions.note: Prototype review: revised presentation continues to conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 21 revised presentation imports standard browser bookmarks, preserves title/tags/dates, converts meaningful folders to tags, and skips duplicates. Client approves.
decisions.note: Prototype review: import behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 21 revised presentation exports `bookmarks.html` in the standard format with titles, tags, and dates. Client approves.
decisions.note: Prototype review: export behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 22 revised presentation supplies default sort, three list-density levels, and text size, persisted across devices. Client says these settings are sufficient for the first build.
decisions.note: Prototype review: personal display settings conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 23 final scope again describes “paste a link” followed by auto-filled details and separately describes editing, retaining the established post-save editor without a pre-save editing step. Client says the complete scope matches without identifying this difference.
decisions.note: Final specification gate: pre-save editing remains absent and passes through bare scope approval.

decisions.evidence: Round 23 final scope includes URL saving, automatic title/description/icon/preview collection, and no duplicates. Client approves the scope.
decisions.note: Final specification gate: the remaining quick-save behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 23 final scope includes editing address/title/description/note/tags, lightweight note formatting, and existing-tag suggestions. Client approves.
decisions.note: Final specification gate: post-save editing, tagging, autocomplete, and Markdown notes conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 23 final scope includes marking links to read later and viewing just those. Client approves the scope.
decisions.note: Final specification gate: unread/read-later behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 23 final scope includes simple search, exact tags, exact phrases, boolean logic, and click-a-tag filtering. Client approves.
decisions.note: Final specification gate: search and tag-filter behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 23 final scope includes sorting by newest, oldest, or title. Client approves.
decisions.note: Final specification gate: sorting conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 23 final scope distinguishes reversible archive from confirmed permanent delete; the previously approved scope includes a separate archive view. Client approves.
decisions.note: Final specification gate: archive and delete behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 23 final scope retains a readable continuous list with long text trimmed. Client approves.
decisions.note: Final specification gate: list presentation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 23 final scope includes multi-select actions and acting on all bookmarks matching a search. Client approves.
decisions.note: Final specification gate: bulk-action scope conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 23 final scope includes named, always-live saved searches. Client approves.
decisions.note: Final specification gate: bundles conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 23 final scope includes automatic preserved copies, real PDFs for PDF URLs, failure/retry, and optional Internet Archive copies. Client specifically authorizes building the actual integrations.
decisions.note: Final specification gate: preservation behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 23 final scope includes standard browser-bookmark import/export with folders mapped to tags and dates retained. Client approves.
decisions.note: Final specification gate: import/export conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 23 final scope includes default sort, list density, and text size synced to the account. Client approves.
decisions.note: Final specification gate: settings conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 24 implementation review instructs the client to paste a URL, wait for auto-filled details, and then explore Edit; it does not present a way to edit title/description before saving. Client accepts the application without surfacing this difference.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the save-first implementation still omits pre-save metadata editing.

decisions.evidence: Round 24 implementation presentation reports the approved quick-save metadata, duplicate handling, post-save editing, notes/tags, unread view, full search language, sorting, archive/delete, bulk actions, live collections, preserved copies, Internet Archive integration, import/export, and settings; client accepts these named areas as complete.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the explicitly presented implemented behaviors conform, apart from the separately recorded pre-save-editing divergence.
